POS refund, approved. Value moving back to the cardholder, so no PIN block. It is a refund from the cardholder's current account. The amount is 2,499.00 PKR. The card number is 4111111111111111, the terminal is POS01993, the acquirer is 0037101, the currency code is 586, and the trace number is 004712. The transmission date and time is 1015093012 (MMDDhhmmss). The account identification is PK12ABCD0000001234.

Give the data elements of the *request* message as a JSON object and nothing else, of the form {"mti": "0200", "fields": {"2": "...", "3": "..."}}. Keys of 'fields' are data element numbers as strings; values are the element contents as strings, already padded to their fixed width where they have one. Do not include a bitmap - it is computed from which elements are present.

The data elements you may need:
  DE 2   Primary account number                     n..19    2-digit length prefix
  DE 3   Processing code                            n6       fixed
  DE 4   Amount, transaction                        n12      fixed
  DE 7   Transmission date and time                 n10      fixed
  DE 11  System trace audit number                  n6       fixed
  DE 12  Local transaction time                     n6       fixed
  DE 13  Local transaction date                     n4       fixed
  DE 14  Expiration date                            n4       fixed
  DE 18  Merchant category code                     n4       fixed
  DE 22  Point of service entry mode                n3       fixed
  DE 25  Point of service condition code            n2       fixed
  DE 32  Acquiring institution identification code  n..11    2-digit length prefix
  DE 33  Forwarding institution identification code n..11    2-digit length prefix
  DE 37  Retrieval reference number                 an12     fixed
  DE 38  Authorization identification response      an6      fixed
  DE 39  Response code                              an2      fixed
  DE 41  Card acceptor terminal identification      ans8     fixed
  DE 42  Card acceptor identification code          ans15    fixed
  DE 43  Card acceptor name and location            ans40    fixed
  DE 49  Currency code, transaction                 n3       fixed
  DE 52  Personal identification number data        b16      fixed
  DE 54  Additional amounts                         an..120  3-digit length prefix
  DE 55  Integrated circuit card data               b..999   3-digit length prefix
  DE 70  Network management information code        n3       fixed
  DE 90  Original data elements                     n42      fixed
  DE 102 Account identification 1                   ans..28  2-digit length prefix
  DE 103 Account identification 2                   ans..28  2-digit length prefix

The invariants this message will be checked against:
  L01  A request is answered or reversed. An unanswered, unreversed financial request is money in an unknown state.
  L02  A response matches a request trace. A response whose DE 11 matches no request cannot be applied to anything.
  L03  A response carries a response code. Without DE 39 the acquirer cannot tell approval from decline.
  L04  The response amount echoes the request. Changing DE 4 outside partial approval silently debits a different amount.
  L05  A partial approval is lower and above zero. DE 39 10 with the full amount is an approval mislabelled, and zero is a decline.
  L06  A reversal carries original data elements. Without DE 90 there is nothing to reverse against.
  L07  DE 90 names a request in this flow. A reversal pointing at an unknown trace reverses nothing and leaves the hold.
  L08  A network message carries DE 70. Sign-on, echo and cutover are told apart only by DE 70.
  L09  The response echoes the account number. A response carrying a different PAN would post to the wrong cardholder.
  L10  The response echoes the processing code. DE 3 decides which account the amount moves from.
  L11  Nothing is reversed after a decline. A decline moved no money, so reversing it can double-credit the cardholder.
  L12  Authorisation approvals carry an id, declines do not. DE 38 is the handle used in disputes; a decline that carries one is ambiguous. Scoped to MTI classes 1 and 2: reversal and network approvals carry no id.
  L13  The response echoes the currency. An amount without its original currency is a settlement break.
  L14  The response echoes terminal and acquirer. These route the response back to the device that is waiting for it.
  L15  No two requests reuse a trace number. A reused DE 11 makes the response ambiguous and breaks reversal matching.
  L16  A cash withdrawal carries a PIN block, a refund does not. Cardholder verification is required one way and forbidden the other.
  L17  An inquiry requests a zero amount. A balance inquiry with a non-zero DE 4 can be posted as a withdrawal.
  L18  A response does not precede its request. Out-of-order traffic means the two were matched by luck, not by trace.
  L19  The account number passes the Luhn check. Every real card number does; one that fails was mistyped or invented.
  L20  Chip tag 9F02 matches the transaction amount. A mismatch debits the cardholder an amount the chip never authorised, and every field is individually well-formed, so nothing else catches it.
  L21  Chip tag 5F2A matches the transaction currency. The chip and the message must agree on what currency was approved.
  L22  Chip data is well-formed and carries the mandatory tags. An authorisation cannot be assessed without the cryptogram, its information data, the counter, the interchange profile and the issuer application data.
